 "summary": "Removes AssumeUTXO snapshot loading, background validation, and multi-chainstate infrastructure across Bitcoin Core. Consolidates ChainstateManager, BlockManager, P2P block downloads, and validation interfaces down to a single active chainstate, eliminating dual block-file cursors, dynamic cache rebalancing, and the loadtxoutset RPC. Leaves UTXO export via dumptxoutset intact while rejecting existing datadirs containing incomplete snapshots at startup.",
 "problem": "Managing multiple concurrent chainstates adds pervasive architectural complexity across validation, memory cache rebalancing, database lifetimes, P2P sync paths, pruning bounds, and wallet rescans. Maintainers bear significant cognitive and code overhead for edge cases in the most critical subsystem of the codebase, which the author argues is no longer justified given low real-world adoption, trust ambiguities with background validation, and performance gains in standard initial block download.",
 "evidence": [
  "PR description: 'Multiple chainstates affect much more than snapshot loading: ordinary validation changes have to account for different chainstate roles, candidate sets, notifications, downloads, pruning, cache allocation, database lifetimes and locks. I am not sure this amount of complexity in the most critical part of our codebase is still worth it, given that adoption isn't where we hoped it would be.'",
  "PR description notes ordinary IBD speed improvements that diminish the payoff of snapshot sync: '#35295 is already merged, and the upcoming pruneassumevalid will make pruned IBD even faster.'"

result.summary: Removes AssumeUTXO snapshot loading, background validation, and multi-chainstate infrastructure across Bitcoin Core. Consolidates ChainstateManager, BlockManager, P2P block downloads, and validation interfaces down to a single active chainstate, eliminating dual block-file cursors, dynamic cache rebalancing, and the loadtxoutset RPC. Leaves UTXO export via dumptxoutset intact while rejecting existing datadirs containing incomplete snapshots at startup.
result.problem: Managing multiple concurrent chainstates adds pervasive architectural complexity across validation, memory cache rebalancing, database lifetimes, P2P sync paths, pruning bounds, and wallet rescans. Maintainers bear significant cognitive and code overhead for edge cases in the most critical subsystem of the codebase, which the author argues is no longer justified given low real-world adoption, trust ambiguities with background validation, and performance gains in standard initial block download.
evidence: PR description: 'Multiple chainstates affect much more than snapshot loading: ordinary validation changes have to account for different chainstate roles, candidate sets, notifications, downloads, pruning, cache allocation, database lifetimes and locks. I am not sure this amount of complexity in the most critical part of our codebase is still worth it, given that adoption isn't where we hoped it would be.'
PR description notes ordinary IBD speed improvements that diminish the payoff of snapshot sync: '#35295 is already merged, and the upcoming pruneassumevalid will make pruned IBD even faster.'
result.scope_notes: Explicit demo PR not intended to be merged as-is; it is an exploration meant to illustrate potential simplifications and inform smaller, targeted PRs.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased onto recent master following the merge of prerequisite #36601.
result.card: This draft demo completely removes AssumeUTXO snapshot loading, background sync, and multi-chainstate architecture across Bitcoin Core to illustrate potential simplifications across validation, block storage, and P2P downloads. It is not intended for merge, but serves as a reference point for carved-out sub-proposals such as dropping background sync or removing dynamic cache resizing. The author argues that pervasive multi-chainstate complexity in the validation engine is no longer justified given low adoption, trust ambiguities, and recent performance gains in standard initial block download.

risk.why: Mistakes in chainstate initialization, block storage cursors, or block download paths could cause node validation crashes, corrupted chainstate, or consensus desync.
